description: 3-position single-row machined-pin (screw-machine) IC/SIP socket strip, 2.54mm (0.1in) pitch, for socketing a TO-92 transistor

evidence.note: Mouser Search API, 2026-09-30: exact match for SS-103-T-2-N (Samtec), Mouser part 200-SS103T2N, description '.100 Single Row Screw Machine Socket Strip'.

Samtec precision-machined-socket-strips catalog page (F-226 supplement, 'SS, SD, ESD, ESS, HSS SERIES', fetched 2026-09-30 from samtec.com - Mouser's own copy of this PDF returns Mouser's Akamai block page, per the sourcing-notes Lessons, so the manufacturer's copy was fetched directly): part-number legend 'TYPE STRIP' digit '1' = single row, then 'NO. PINS PER ROW' 01 thru 32 as a two-digit field - SS-103 parses as SS + type-strip '1' + pin count '03', i.e. 3 positions.

Samtec precision-machined-socket-strips catalog page (fetched 2026-09-30): header '(2.54 mm) .100"' and dimension drawing '(2.54) .100 x No. of Positions' for the SS/ESS single-row series; same page states 'Lead Size Range: (0.38mm to 0.56mm) .015" to .022" DIA and most all IC leads', which covers a TO-92 lead (about 0.41-0.53mm per onsemi's TO-92 dimension table).

why: A native 3-position single-row machined-pin socket strip - no need to break a longer strip down to size. Samtec SS (standard height) is preferred over the otherwise-identical ESS (elevated) series at this position count: cheaper (about $0.76 each in ones vs $1.52 for ESS-103-T-08) and lower-profile, which suits a bench/perfboard build. Both are 'screw machine' (machined-pin) construction, not stamped. Amazon was not used: the sourcing notes restrict Amazon/marketplace sourcing to parts where a counterfeit does not matter, and a real per-pin datasheet (Samtec's) was readable and gave a clear position-count and pitch match, so Mouser was used instead.
